open_questions: Duration ratio 1.664 (TIC) to 1.5 (Gaia FLAME/GSP-Phot 0.452/0.455 Rsun) and fit_log_density_ratio -1.794 with star_density_penalty 728.1 imply a long/low-density fit for a 0.41-0.45 Rsun M dwarf; eccentricity or spot-induced shape not constrained by TESS alone

Phase-curve amplitude 8067 ppm (ratio_to_depth 1.346, chi2 481.1 dof 9) implies strong variability at the 0.69249 d period exactly matching the signal; stellar activity vs eccentric/close planet cannot be separated here, follow-up photometry needed
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a steady 0.69-day dip centred on the M dwarf in 67 transits with no odd/even change or secondary eclipse, and a planet-sized radius of about 3.5 Earth radii. A large brightness swing at the same period is seen, and the transit is longer than expected for the star, but both can be explained by planet plus stellar activity. The best explanation remains a small planet on target.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target in both sectors used, excluding the 6 neighbours that could cause it (plausible_within_1px 0, closest suspects >72 sigma away). Favours planet on target over a blended binary.
No significant V-shape; flat bottom with fit_b 0.005455 argues against grazing binary, consistent with small-planet transit.
Odd and even depths identical (odd 5439 ppm vs even 5443 ppm, ratio 1) excludes eclipsing binary at twice the period.
No secondary dip at any phase (depth_ppm -283.5) and snr below 5, negative secondary_over_bump -0.07726, no close binary eclipse.
Depth steady across sectors (20: 5450 ppm, 47: 5433 ppm, chi2 0.0006531, dof 1) with 67 transits (refit snr 26.41) and ingress fraction 0.2; not a few bad events.
Planet-sized signal, much below star regime, and neighbours could_cause_within_1px 0 so no blend dilation.

dossier.xgboost.planet_rank: 0.2 (low), dragged down by duration/radius mismatch and strong phase curve; flat-bottom, on-target, steady, secondary-free evidence outweighs it.
